title: Heels vs Sneaker Utilization Split
dataSources: Closet activity (`style:wardrobe`), cleaning tasks (`style:cleaning`), shoe wears (`style:shoes`), beauty inventory (`beauty:product`), audits (`style:audit`).
app: Wardrobe and beauty telemetry — Stylebook closet exports, dry-cleaning reminders, shoe-rotation logs, and makeup inventory audits — streamed to Splunk HEC via exports and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=style:shoes shoe_family=*
| stats count as items by shoe_family
| eventstats sum(items) as total
| eval share_pct=round(100*items/total,1)
| sort - share_pct
description: Shows how shoe wears split across shoe family for footwear use balance.
value: Share-of-total views make it easier to see imbalance, over-concentration, and neglected areas inside footwear use balance.
implementation: Capture each shoe wears event in `style:shoes` and normalize `shoe_family` so Splunk can compute the share by shoe family.
visualization: Table of shoe family with item count and share percentage.
grandmaExplanation: It turns how shoe wears are divided across shoe family so you can tell if one part of footwear use balance is taking over.
